name: Toyota Corolla
title: Toyota Corolla Problems by Year: Years to Avoid and What Owners Report | Steer Me Right
description: Which Toyota Corolla model years to buy used and which to skip, from NHTSA owner complaints per 100,000 sold, recalls by year, the 2020 stalling fix and what owners report on Reddit.
h1: Toyota Corolla problems by year: years to avoid and what owners report
card: The best and worst Corolla years, the 2020 stalling and fuel pump fixes, complaints per 100,000 sold and what owners report.
answer: The best used Corollas are the 2022 to 2025 model years, which draw {r:2022}, {r:2023}, {r:2024} and {r:2025} NHTSA owner complaints per 100,000 sold against a Corolla yardstick of {base}, and the 2016 to 2018 also rate Buy, at {r:2016}, {r:2017} and {r:2018}. Skip the 2020: it draws {r:2020} per 100,000, with {k:2020:ENGINE} of its {c:2020} complaints naming the engine, and it needed a software fix for stalling as well as a fuel pump recall. The 2019 ({r:2019}) and 2021 ({r:2021}) are the years in between; {k:2021:AIR BAGS} of the 2021’s {c:2021} complaints name air bags, which recall 23V-865 covers.

The rates divide each model year’s NHTSA complaints, counted across the Corolla, Corolla Hybrid, Corolla Hatchback, Corolla iM and GR Corolla listings, by U.S. sales. The 2026 has no complaints on NHTSA’s list yet and is too new to rate. Our Corolla price guide covers what a new or used one costs and also says to skip the 2020.
salesNote: Sales come from Good Car Bad Car’s Corolla table, which our Corolla vs Elantra page also uses; its 2023 to 2025 total is one unit under Toyota’s year-end releases.

2016: Air bags ({k:2016:AIR BAGS}) lead a modest count. Recall 20V-024 covers an air bag control unit that can fail in some crashes on 2011 to 2019 Corollas.
2017: Air bags ({k:2017:AIR BAGS}) lead again, with speed control ({k:2017:VEHICLE SPEED CONTROL}) next. Recalls 17V-295 (spare tire pressure) and 20V-024 apply.
2018: The fuel system ({k:2018:FUEL/PROPULSION SYSTEM}) and air bags ({k:2018:AIR BAGS}) lead a small count. Recall 20V-024 applies.
2019: Power train ({k:2019:POWER TRAIN}), fuel system ({k:2019:FUEL/PROPULSION SYSTEM}) and engine ({k:2019:ENGINE}) lead. Recalls 18V-901 (hatchback CVT), 20V-012 and 20V-682 (fuel pump) apply.
2020: Engine ({k:2020:ENGINE}) leads, ahead of power train ({k:2020:POWER TRAIN}). Toyota’s campaign 22TC07 fixes stalling, and recalls 20V-682 (fuel pump), 19V-877 and 23V-865 apply.
2021: Air bags ({k:2021:AIR BAGS}) and engine ({k:2021:ENGINE}) lead. Recall 23V-865 covers the passenger occupant sensor on 2020 and 2021 cars; ask for proof.
2022: A small count ({c:2022}) led by electrical, power train and brakes, and {rec:2022} recalls on NHTSA’s list.
2023: {c:2023} complaints. Six recalls include the steering column cable (23V-480, 25V-040), the steering shaft (24V-878) and the Hybrid’s brake software (24V-708).
2024: {c:2024} complaints. Recalls 24V-878 (steering shaft) and 24V-708 (Hybrid brake software) apply.
2025: The lowest rate of any year, with {c:2025} complaints. Hybrid brake software recall 24V-708 applies.
2026: {c:2026} complaints on NHTSA’s list and {rec:2026} recall (26V-110, headlight aim markings). Too new to rate.

chartNote: The 2020 bar is the tallest, and {k:2020:ENGINE} of its complaints name the engine.

generations.name: Eleventh generation
generations.text: The 2014 to 2019 Corolla sedan used a 1.8-liter four-cylinder (132 hp, and 140 hp on the LE Eco), with a CVT, a four-speed automatic on the base L and a six-speed manual on the L and S. A 2017 refresh brought a new front end, a 7-inch touchscreen and the SE and XSE trims (Wikipedia).

generations.name: Twelfth generation
generations.text: The hatchback arrived first, for 2019, and the sedan followed for 2020, with a 2.0-liter engine (169 hp) on SE and XSE, a 1.8-liter (139 hp) below them and a 121-hp 1.8-liter hybrid, the first Corolla hybrid sold here. A refresh for 2023 put the 2.0-liter and a CVT on every gas model, dropped the manual, added all-wheel drive to the hybrid and made Toyota Safety Sense 3.0 standard (Wikipedia).

problems.title: Engine, 2020 and 2021
problems.text: NHTSA’s field doesn’t say what owners describe. Toyota’s software campaign 22TC07 fixes stalling on the 2020, according to our Civic vs Corolla page. It is a service campaign and not a recall, so a VIN lookup won’t show it.

problems.title: Fuel system, 2018 to 2020
problems.text: Recall 20V-012 covers an in-tank low-pressure fuel pump that can fail and stall the engine on 2019 Corollas, and 20V-682 on 2019 hatchbacks and 2020 cars. Dealers replace the pump assembly free.

problems.title: Air bags, 2016 to 2021
problems.text: Recall 20V-024 covers an air bag control unit that can malfunction in certain crashes on 2011 to 2019 Corollas; dealers install a noise filter free. Recall 23V-865 covers a passenger occupant sensor that can short and stop the air bag deploying on 2020 and 2021 cars.

problems.title: Power train, 2019 and 2020
problems.text: Recall 18V-901 covers a torque converter in 2019 hatchbacks with the CVT whose impeller blades can detach and stall the car; dealers replace the CVT and converter free. No recall names the power train on the sedans.

problems.title: Steering, 2023 and 2024
problems.text: Recall 24V-878 covers a steering intermediate shaft that can crack and detach on 2023 and 2024 Corollas, and 23V-480 and 25V-040 a steering column cable that can deactivate the driver’s air bag on 2023 cars. Dealers replace the parts free.

paragraphs: Reddit owners report Corollas lasting 200,000 to 300,000 miles on routine maintenance, and say the hybrid and CVT drivetrains hold up when the fluid is changed on schedule. The complaints are older engines burning oil or losing a head gasket, CVT trouble on some newer cars and coolant bypass valve failures on twelfth-generation cars. NHTSA’s field doesn’t say whether the 2020’s engine complaints are about that valve.

notableRecalls.title: Air bag control unit
notableRecalls.text: The air bag control unit may malfunction in certain crashes and keep the air bags or seat belt pretensioners from deploying. Dealers install a noise filter free.

notableRecalls.title: In-tank fuel pump
notableRecalls.text: The low-pressure pump can fail and stall the engine. Dealers replace the pump assembly with an improved one, free.

notableRecalls.title: Torque converter impeller
notableRecalls.text: The impeller blades can detach under high load and stall a CVT car. Dealers replace the CVT and torque converter free.

notableRecalls.title: Passenger occupant sensor
notableRecalls.text: A short circuit in the sensor can keep the front passenger air bag from deploying. Dealers inspect and replace it free.

notableRecalls.title: Rear seat belt lock
notableRecalls.text: The rear seat belt webbing sensor may not lock as intended in a crash with several impacts. Dealers replace the assemblies as needed, free.

notableRecalls.title: Steering column cable
notableRecalls.text: A weak weld inside the spiral cable can separate and deactivate the driver’s air bag; 25V-040 covers cars repaired incorrectly under 23V-480. Dealers replace the cable free.

notableRecalls.title: Steering intermediate shaft
notableRecalls.text: Cracks from manufacturing can make the shaft fracture and detach from the steering column. Dealers replace it free.

notableRecalls.title: Brake assist software
notableRecalls.text: A software error can cut power brake assist when turning a corner. Dealers update the brake computer free.

notableRecalls.title: Headlight aim markings
notableRecalls.text: The front headlights may lack aim markings, which can leave them aimed wrongly after service. Dealers replace both assemblies free.

noInvestigations: NHTSA has no open investigation on the 2016 to 2026 Corolla as of November 21, 2026. The only item on its list that names the Corolla, EQ21001, is closed and covers replacement air bag modules in 2003 to 2008 cars.

checks.title: Stalling and fuel pump fixes on a 2019 or 2020.
checks.text: Confirm recalls 20V-012 and 20V-682 are closed, and ask whether Toyota’s stalling campaign 22TC07 was done on a 2020. It is not a recall, so the VIN lookup won’t show it.

checks.title: CVT recall on a 2019 hatchback.
checks.text: Confirm 18V-901 is closed; the repair replaces the CVT and torque converter.

checks.title: Air bag recalls on a 2016 to 2021.
checks.text: Confirm 20V-024 on a 2016 to 2019 and 23V-865 on a 2020 or 2021. Both are free at a Toyota dealer.

checks.title: Steering recalls on a 2023 or 2024.
checks.text: Ask for proof that 24V-878 (steering shaft) is done and, on a 2023, that 23V-480 and 25V-040 are closed.

checks.title: Coolant and oil on a 2020.
checks.text: Reddit owners report coolant bypass valve failures on twelfth-generation cars and older engines burning oil. Check the coolant level, look for leaks and read the oil level.

checks.title: An independent inspection.
checks.text: Have a shop that isn’t the seller’s check the engine and transmission before you sign, especially on a 2020.

newer: The 2026 Corolla has {c:2026} complaints on NHTSA’s list and {rec:2026} recall so far, for headlight aim markings, and it is too new to rate. If you are choosing between a new 2026 and a used 2024 or 2025, the used cars carry steering shaft recall 24V-878 (2024) and Hybrid brake software recall 24V-708.
Our Corolla price guide has the 2026 prices, Toyota’s financing and our take on buying new.
faq: What is the worst Toyota Corolla year?
The 2020, at {r:2020} NHTSA complaints per 100,000 sold on {c:2020} complaints, {k:2020:ENGINE} of them naming the engine. It needed a software fix for stalling and a fuel pump recall.
What is the best used Corolla year?
The 2022 to 2025 model years, at {r:2022}, {r:2023}, {r:2024} and {r:2025} complaints per 100,000. The 2016 to 2018 also rate Buy, at {r:2016}, {r:2017} and {r:2018}.

Reddit owners report 200,000 to 300,000 miles on routine maintenance. NHTSA’s counts rate seven of the ten model years from 2016 to 2025 Buy, against a Corolla yardstick of {base} complaints per 100,000.
Did Toyota recall the 2019 and 2020 Corolla for the fuel pump?
Yes. Recalls 20V-012 and 20V-682 cover an in-tank fuel pump that can fail and stall the engine, and the repair is free at a Toyota dealer. A VIN lookup shows whether it is still open.
How do I check a used Corolla for recalls?
Enter the VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. It lists open recalls for that car, and recall repairs are free at a Toyota dealer.
